podcast.body: Originally demoed by Prince in 1984 and recorded by his funk band, The Family, in 1985, this song was suggested to Sinead by her manager Steve Fargnoli. Engineer Chris Birkett produced the track, which was recorded with a hi-hat loop, programmed strings, and notably no bass. Sinead recorded the vocal in one take using Birkett's "go-to mic," an AKG 414B, and then double-tracked it perfectly. The accompanying music video, mostly filmed in London and featuring genuine tears, helped propel the song to number one globally after initially struggling. "But the vocal went down extraordinarily in one take."

podcast.body: Sinéad O'Connor's "totemic" 1990 cover of Prince's heartbreak ballad, which reached number one. This was one of several straightforward covers that achieved chart-topping success during the late 1980s and early 1990s. "Shaneid O'Connor's Tohtemic 1990 cover of Prince's Heartbreak Ballad, Nothing Comparious To You."

podcast.body: The video for "Nothing Compares 2 U" featured a simple headshot of Sinéad O'Connor singing. Despite its visual simplicity, it is remembered as one of the truly great music videos from the "glory years" of the 1980s and 1990s. "The simple headshot of Shenato Conor singing Nothing compares to you."
